name: Hadatai bodysuit

card.summary: A skin-tone full-body zentai suit worn under kigurumi masks so the performer appears as a smooth, stylised anime character.
card.note: Costume item for masked cosplay; not a body-shaping or medical product.

quick.overview:
A hadatai is a flesh-coloured zentai bodysuit, a stretch garment covering the whole body, used in kigurumi (animegao) masked cosplay. Paired with a moulded mask, it gives a uniform, doll-like or animated skin surface with no visible detail of the wearer.

The look is stylised rather than realistic: performers add padding, breast forms or binders to match a character's silhouette, so the suit works as the base layer of a transformation into a character.
quick.how: Wearers put on the suit, add shaping pieces to match the character's body, then wear costume and wig with a mask. Some hadatai have a face opening for the mask; the style can leave no skin exposed.
quick.risks: Full-body suits and masks restrict ventilation and vision and can cause overheating. Some places restrict face coverings in public (for example France, per general zentai coverage).

lead: Hadatai (skin-tone bodysuits) are a type of zentai, the Japanese term derived from 'zenshin taitsu', meaning full-body tights, typically made of nylon-spandex blends.[2] In kigurumi, also called animegao ('anime face'), performers wear a plastic mask with a flesh-coloured bodysuit that often has an opening for the face, and add breast forms, chest binders and hip padding to match a character's body shape.[1]

The suit and mask together give a smooth, animation-like appearance with less detail than normal skin and facial features. The practice began in official Japanese anime stage shows, was taken up by hobbyists, and drew attention in North America and Europe around 2005.[1]

chain: Skin-tone suit covers the whole body
Uniform surface hides the wearer's own features
Mask and padding present a stylised character figure
angle.text: It creates a seamless, smooth skin surface for a character appearance, and is the base layer on which masks, wigs and shaping pieces sit.

paras: Zentai suits are skin-tight garments covering the whole body, used by sports fans, dancers, video effects crews (solid colours suit chroma key) and others.[2] The hadatai variant uses a flesh tone so that, under a mask, no obvious skin or clothing line shows.[1]

Kigurumi performers usually depict established anime, game or manga characters, most often female and human, though male, mechanical and original characters also appear, and wearing it is not limited to one gender.[1] Masks are moulded or 3D-printed, sourced from specialised studios, and custom masks with wigs and eyes cost roughly 100,000 to 200,000 yen as of 2018.[1]
Kigurumi has appeared in performance, photography and fashion, in Japanese kigurumi cafes and in music videos.[1]

timeline.event: Kigurumi gains attention in North America and Europe.[1]
